evidence: createApp registers Express routes and delegates each operation to service.createUser, createProject, createTask, listTasks and markDone. This is transport adapter work, which belongs in infrastructure.
bodyOf and stringField only coerce the shape of request input. They contain no domain validation.
statusCode(error) maps DomainError.code to 404, 409 or 400, which turns domain errors into HTTP responses and belongs in the transport layer.
The default parameter of createApp, new TaskService(new InMemoryTaskRepository()), is composition-root wiring, which belongs in infrastructure.
The route handlers cast status with `as TaskStatus` but enforce no rules themselves, so business validation stays in the application or domain layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-server.ts is an HTTP transport adapter, and everything in it fits the infrastructure layer. bodyOf and stringField parse and coerce request input, and the route handlers turn request bodies and query strings into application DTOs (CreateTaskInput, TaskFilter). The handlers then call TaskService methods and write the results as HTTP responses with status codes. statusCode() and the error middleware turn DomainError codes into HTTP statuses, which is transport work. The default parameter in createApp wires TaskService to an InMemoryTaskRepository, which is composition-root work that belongs in infrastructure. The file contains no business rules: it doesn't validate titles, enforce status transitions, check assignees or detect conflicts. It hands all of that to the application service. It also has no persistence logic of its own.
